title: Posting an assessment
lede: Normally OME does this. It is documented here so you know what is being set on your behalf, and what cannot be changed afterwards.

blocks.title: Who posts
blocks.text: OME pre-clerkship staff post assessments as part of the preparation window. Do not post your own exam unless OME has specifically asked you to. If you do, every field below matters.
Posting is what opens the download window. Open the assessment, scroll to the end, and select **Post Assessment**. A dialog opens with the fields below.

blocks.caption: Posting fields and the JABSOM convention for each
rows: The exam name as students should see it
This is the label that appears on the student iPad for download and during the exam.
Minimum 6 letters plus at least 1 number
Required. The proctor announces it at exam time. It is never emailed to students.
The correct course for the cohort
Drives enrolment and reporting. The wrong course posts the exam to the wrong students.
Gives students time to download onto the iPad. JABSOM posts 36 to 48 hours ahead.
30 minutes to 1 hour after the exam
Covers late arrivals and device swaps without leaving the window open.
A JABSOM standing rule. It prevents a student re-downloading onto a second device.
Appears on the posting and in reporting.
Automated nudge to download before the window closes.
Automated nudge to upload the answer file after the exam.
Optional, but good practice to set it
Late uploads are flagged, which makes exceptions easy to spot.
Unless your course has specifically planned an in-room review.
JABSOM does not use them for standard pre-clerkship exams.

blocks.title: Max Downloads is always 1
blocks.text: Of every field on this dialog, this is the one that is a hard JABSOM convention rather than a judgement call. It has been 1 in every onboarding document since 2020.

blocks.title: After posting plus one download, the content is frozen
blocks.text: Once the assessment is posted **and at least one student has downloaded it**, questions and answer keys can no longer be altered. If you find an error after that point it becomes a post-exam scoring adjustment, not an edit. Catch content problems during the OME proofing window.

blocks.title: Never send the password to students
blocks.text: When an assessment is posted, a general notification email usually goes out so students know it is available to download. The exam password is not in it and must not be. The proctor announces the password in the room at exam time.
